# Broken cipher, ECB mode or unpadded RSA (Java)

`qualor:java/weak-cipher` · Issue · Severity: Medium · [CWE-327](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/327.html) · OWASP Top 10: [A04:2025 Cryptographic Failures](https://top10.owasp.org/2025/A04_2025-Cryptographic_Failures/), [A02:2021 Cryptographic Failures](https://top10.owasp.org/2021/A02_2021-Cryptographic_Failures/)

## What it finds

<!-- begin: what-it-finds -->
JCA `Cipher.getInstance` transformations that do not protect the data, named by a literal or a
constant:

- the algorithms DES, DESede (Triple DES, also `TripleDES` and `DESedeWrap`), RC2, RC4
  (`ARCFOUR`) and Blowfish, in any mode, and the password-based names built on them
  (`PBEWithMD5AndDES`, `PBEWithSHA1AndDESede`, `PBEWithSHA1AndRC4_128`, ...);
- ECB mode with a block cipher (`AES/ECB/PKCS5Padding`), and `AES` named without a mode, which
  the JDK's providers then run in ECB mode;
- RSA without padding (`RSA/ECB/NoPadding`);
- `new NullCipher()`, which does not encrypt at all.

Names are compared without regard to case, as the JCA does. `AES/GCM/NoPadding`,
`ChaCha20-Poly1305`, RSA with OAEP or PKCS #1 padding, the key-wrap ciphers and names read from
configuration are not reported. Test code is skipped: the `src/test/` tree
(also `src/testFixtures/`, `src/integrationTest/` and `src/intTest/`) and files whose names end
in `Test`, `Tests`, `TestCase`, `IT` or `ITCase`.
<!-- end: what-it-finds -->

## Why it matters

<!-- begin: why-it-matters -->
DES has a 56-bit key that can be found by brute force; RC4's output is biased enough to recover
plaintext; Triple DES, RC2 and Blowfish have 64-bit blocks, so after a few gigabytes under one key
blocks collide and leak data (birthday-bound attacks). ECB encrypts equal blocks to equal
ciphertext, so patterns in the data stay visible (the JCA names page: ECB "generally ... should
not be used for multiple blocks of data"), and `AES` alone means ECB with the JDK's providers. RSA
without padding is deterministic and malleable. None of these keep the data confidential, and none
of them detect changes to it.
<!-- end: why-it-matters -->

## Example

<!-- begin: example -->
**Noncompliant:** `AES` without a mode is AES in ECB mode.

```java
package com.example.vault;

import java.security.GeneralSecurityException;
import javax.crypto.Cipher;
import javax.crypto.SecretKey;

public class Vault {
    public static byte[] seal(SecretKey key, byte[] data) throws GeneralSecurityException {
        Cipher cipher = Cipher.getInstance("AES");
        cipher.init(Cipher.ENCRYPT_MODE, key);
        return cipher.doFinal(data);
    }
}
```

**Compliant:** AES in GCM mode, with a fresh nonce for every message.

```java
package com.example.vault;

import java.nio.ByteBuffer;
import java.security.GeneralSecurityException;
import java.security.SecureRandom;
import javax.crypto.Cipher;
import javax.crypto.SecretKey;
import javax.crypto.spec.GCMParameterSpec;

public class Vault {
    private static final SecureRandom RANDOM = new SecureRandom();

    public static byte[] seal(SecretKey key, byte[] data) throws GeneralSecurityException {
        byte[] nonce = new byte[12];
        RANDOM.nextBytes(nonce);
        Cipher cipher = Cipher.getInstance("AES/GCM/NoPadding");
        cipher.init(Cipher.ENCRYPT_MODE, key, new GCMParameterSpec(128, nonce));
        byte[] sealed = cipher.doFinal(data);
        return ByteBuffer.allocate(nonce.length + sealed.length).put(nonce).put(sealed).array();
    }
}
```
<!-- end: example -->

## How to fix

<!-- begin: how-to-fix -->
- Encrypt with an authenticated cipher and write the mode and padding out:
  `Cipher.getInstance("AES/GCM/NoPadding")` with a new 12-byte nonce for every message, or
  `Cipher.getInstance("ChaCha20-Poly1305")`.
- For RSA, use OAEP: `RSA/ECB/OAEPWithSHA-256AndMGF1Padding` (the `ECB` in RSA names is nominal).
- For password-based encryption, derive a key with PBKDF2 and encrypt with AES-GCM, or use a
  `PBEWithHmacSHA256AndAES_256` name.
- Data already encrypted with an old cipher: decrypt it once and encrypt it again with the new one;
  keep the old cipher in that migration code only.
<!-- end: how-to-fix -->

## Frameworks and APIs covered

- `javax.crypto`

## Known limits

<!-- begin: known-limits -->
- Only names the code holds as constants are checked: a name chosen by a condition or passed to a
  helper that creates the cipher is missed, and so is a name read from configuration, even when
  the lookup's default is weak (`getProperty(key, "DESede/ECB/PKCS5Padding")`): the configured
  value decides. On the OWASP Benchmark (crypto) the rule finds 97 of the 130 real cases, with no
  false positive; the 33 it misses take a configured name whose default is Triple DES.
- Only the JCA `Cipher` API is checked: Bouncy Castle's lightweight engines (`DESEngine`,
  `RC4Engine`, ...) are not.
- ECB on a single block (wrapping one AES key with `AES/ECB/NoPadding`), which the JCA names page
  allows, is still reported.
- Unauthenticated modes such as AES in CBC or CTR mode, and RSA with PKCS #1 v1.5 padding, are not
  reported.
- Skipping test code by file name also skips a production class whose name ends in `Test` or `IT`.
<!-- end: known-limits -->

lines marked `ruleid:` must be reported and lines marked `ok:` must not. The known limits are
marked `todoruleid:` (missed) and `todook:` (wrongly reported). `npm test` runs them with OpenGrep,
and checks the example above as well.
